workstreams.name: Phase 0: foundations
workstreams.covers: Engine pinned to the Showdown server commit, tests migrated, 29,404 real replays admitted, benchmark harness.

workstreams.name: Your own moves
workstreams.covers: Which moves you have, their PP and when it is fresh, and disabled / trapped / locked moves.

workstreams.name: Your own leftovers and decision points
workstreams.covers: What kind of decision point this is (normal, forced switch, end of battle), and the unresolved EV/IV and random-gender questions.

workstreams.name: Who is who on the field
workstreams.covers: Which Pokemon is really in play after switches, U-turn, Roar, Illusion and Transform: roster, slot, team size, party order, appearance, form, types and Tera, plus opponent details. Every later public fact depends on this.

workstreams.name: HP, status and boosts
workstreams.covers: Opponent HP, fainting and status; how long a status has lasted (sleep, toxic counters); stat boosts for both sides.

workstreams.name: Items and abilities
workstreams.covers: Items (identity, held, active) for both sides; opponent ability and whether abilities are active.

workstreams.name: Effects with a lifetime
workstreams.covers: Volatiles (Substitute, Leech Seed, Taunt...), single-turn effects (Protect), single-move effects (Destiny Bond), hazards and screens with layers, weather / terrain / Trick Room with turns left, and pending effects (Future Sight, Wish).

workstreams.name: Move history
workstreams.covers: Which moves each Pokemon has used, including copied moves (Mimic, Sketch, Transform).

workstreams.name: Replay ingestion
workstreams.covers: Real replays run through the same knowledge path as self-play; the old unsafe replay tools are retired.

workstreams.name: Publication to Python
workstreams.covers: Full knowledge snapshots to Python with tamper checks. W9-lite (decision frames) is done.

workstreams.name: Final assurance
workstreams.covers: Registry at zero missing, one end-to-end test from battle start to end for both players, final review.

workstreams.name: Track B: learned models
workstreams.covers: Features, dataset, imitation model, search, self-play. B1 code is committed.

pace: When a slice is being worked on, it is fast: most go from brief to accepted in under two hours (see the slice table).

Most of the calendar time is waiting: long corpus runs (downloads, 3.5 h sample gates, 24-37 h full-corpus runs that were planned and then stopped), plus the time between sessions. Every handoff between Claude and Codex goes through the owner.

Most slices so far built infrastructure, not knowledge. Of 21 slices, only W1.2 and W1.3 adopted new knowledge rows (+13). P0.5c1's +16 was reclassification. Phase 0 and the born-session / switch-authority work were prerequisites.
Before 2026-10-16, the Prompt-era process (Prompts 1-62, about 1,350 planning and evidence files, 44 MB) ended with 9 adopted rows. That ceremony was dropped for the lean process.
The hard part is ahead: 75 rows missing and 7 blocked, including 26 effect-ledger rows (W6, 8-12 slices). The plan estimates about 25-40 more Track A slices.

Scope note: no opponent (public) row is adopted yet, but the public readers behind the v2 observation already match the simulator (0 mismatches in 123.6M checks). The 2026-10-26 plan reuses them: each public row must equal simulator truth, agree with v2 where v2 has the field, and never be known before its reveal. That should make public rows cheaper than the own-side W1 rows were.
Known gap (found 2026-10-26): the v2 public view does not carry the opponent's revealed moves, ability, item or Tera type.
